baseline_gamma_vs_gamma_across_studies.note: hugely dispersed -- OSD-498 and OSD-508 are two accessions of the same published experiment and correlate at 0.07, so full-profile correlation is dominated by study-level noise

excluded_studies.OSD-658: irradiated dry dormant seed; every other study used hydrated seedlings or plants, so its divergence confounds tissue state with radiation quality and cannot support a quality claim

interpretation: NOT SUPPORTED. The matched within-OSD-320 comparison of gamma against Fe-56 HZE gives rho 0.31, which sits at the 20.0th percentile of the gamma-versus-gamma baseline (mean 0.43, range [0.068, 0.661]; one-sided p = 0.25). The variation between two gamma irradiations in different laboratories -- and even between two accessions of the same experiment, which correlate at 0.07 -- is as large as the difference between low-LET photons and high-LET particles. These data therefore do NOT support radiation quality as the reason spaceflight shows no signature, and the argument rests on dose: the model was trained at 100 Gy while the ISS delivers at most 2.485 cGy, a factor of ~4024. All radiation qualities fire both arms of the decoder, which is consistent with a conserved DNA-damage core.

matched_pair_vs_baseline.criterion: quality claim requires the matched pair in the lower tail (p < 0.05), not merely below the baseline mean

matched_test.design: same study, same 6-day seedlings, same facility (BNL), same dose rate and harvest times; Cs-137 gamma (100 Gy) vs 1 GeV/n Fe-56 HZE (30 Gy)
